title: Matched population comparison of visual outcomes and patient satisfaction between 3 modalities for the correction of low to moderate myopic astigmatism

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 (article <license>: Dove Medical Press terms incorporating the Creative Commons Attribution - Non Commercial (unported, v3.0) License)

indication: low to moderate myopic astigmatism (inclusion: SE -3 to -8 D, astigmatism at least -0.75 D, age 21-40 years); prospective non-randomized single-centre comparison of T-ICL, femto-LASIK and ReLEx SMILE

groups.description: Group B femto-LASIK: VisuMax flap 100-120 um, MEL 90 standard (non-wavefront) ablation with iris recognition, aim of emmetropia; bilateral surgery, one eye per patient analysed
Group C ReLEx SMILE: VisuMax 500 kHz, cap 120 um, 2 mm incision, manual cyclotorsion compensation; bilateral surgery, one eye per patient analysed

series.notes: mean ± SD; per-group n not tabulated (Methods: 30 eyes of 30 patients; the reported percentages of eyes are consistent only with 30 eyes per group); per-visit n not reported
mean ± SD; per-group n not tabulated (as for FS-LASIK); per-visit n not reported

exclusions.reason: toric phakic intraocular lens, out of scope

notes: Refraction: manifest refraction at each visit from 1 month onward (Methods); recorded as manifest. Day 1 and 1 week visits are not tabulated.
Target: stated as emmetropia for femto-LASIK; not stated for SMILE (recorded as unstated).
Groups were matched by the authors for age, SE, contrast sensitivity and TBUT; one eye per patient was included although surgery was bilateral.
UDVA, CDVA, cylinder (Table 2), HOA, endothelial cell density, TBUT and contrast sensitivity (Table 4) are tabulated; not extracted.
